## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Syntakt

- **C8** (C) Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken. dnfw's LFO4 bridge passed every check and then faulted on a Digitone II. Three checks had reported success about work they never did: snapshot harnesses cleared code that no real boot had run; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after an unrelated edit had deleted its coverage section; and an emulator call returned 0 for a value that was present. Use a key nothing set that must read back absent, a routine list that must not be empty, a coverage line that must appear. A green result from an untested instrument is not evidence. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4} Incidents: [I42](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i42-checks-reported-success-about-work-they-never-did). Test a safety mechanism's first step end to end through the production code: Synfact's safe-boot trial passed unit tests that replaced the eMMC write with a double, then crashed every boot on a Syntakt because the real table had no write function. Incidents: [I62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i62-a-safe-boot-trial-crashed-every-boot), [I56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). For UI lifecycle tests, replay the actual edit and its notifications without manually repairing the next view. Armio's sampler tests explicitly reselected SYN before turning the sample knob; that hid a Machine-change path which left the old view attached. The corrected replay fails on R020 and passes the R021/R022 fix. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines).

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Syntakt (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`): if the OS still boots, flash the stock `.syx` via Transfer's Drop page (works even if a mod misbehaved); if not, MIDI interface with a 5-pin OUT to the Syntakt's MIDI IN ("USB doesn't work from the startup menu"), FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, Transfer SYSEX TRANSFER "OS Upgrade via device startup menu", tens of minutes at 31.25 kbit/s, the unit restarts itself. Avoid TRIG 2 (empty reset) and TRIG 3 (factory reset) in the startup menu - both erase data. Do a dry run of the DIN procedure with the stock OS before the first flash; flash only files for which `tools/unpack/eft.py info <file>` reports `checksums : ok`; no hardware results are reported on the page. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery} (`recovery#2934ea2d`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L36))

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I20** Mod code at a "free" address crashed projects with certain samples. Cause: mod code at `0x46000000`, memory stock uses for those samples. Fix: v0.8.1 unpacks the mod code into a 64 KB block that a hook at the end of heap init (`0x4010358E`) reserves first. Rules: D11.
- **I50** Mod data written for default settings slowed project load and save. Cause: the ARP mod sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; the project itself was valid. Fix: leave the carrier absent while all thirteen rows are defaults: 81 % fewer emulated instructions for a full serialization. Rules: E4.
- **I62** A safe-boot trial crashed every boot. Cause: the boot's eMMC accessor table had no write function, so marking the bank TRYING called address 0; the record never changed, so every boot retried the same bank. The unit tests had replaced exactly this piece with doubles. Fix: core 1.7.1 adds the write function, storage fails closed on a table without one, and an end-to-end test through the production loader reproduces the crash. Rules: C8.
- **I63** A mod's memory window broke the BASE/WDTH filter. Cause: the stock base-width filter reads Q31 poles from a 508-entry table with a zero tail and indexes up to 1023; Synfact's companion window sat in that tail, so BASE+WDTH of 128 or more read code as poles. Fix: core 1.7.2 bounds the index to 508. Rules: A43.
- **I64** A chorus running from DDR overloaded the Syntakt's MAIN CPU. Cause: all chorus code ran from DDR; about 5.4 KB of code was fetched per block. Fix: 0.2 moved the hot code and kernels into MAIN SRAM (0.2 KB fetched per block). Rules: A34.
- **I46** Syntakt startup-menu recovery tested over DIN. Cause: test. Fix: — Rules: A11,A36.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O1** Syntakt OS signing: A) SyntHack OS: 1.41 carries an HMAC-SHA256, with the key derived from the image B) digikit finding 70: 1.42 has no HMAC trailer (the last 32 bytes are zero)
- **O3** Syntakt CPU #1 load: A) ~89 % of the audio interrupt at rest (SyntHack, measured with DTIM0) B) the render is 85.8k of 166.7k cycles per block (SY FM4)

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **T4** (needs unit + SyntHack, effort M) Measure CPU #1 load with the digihealth DMA-timer method over the whole interrupt, at rest and busy
- **T5** (needs files, effort S) Check the trailer and HMAC of 1.40A/1.41/1.42 with your own files (elektron-firmware-tool, digikit)
- **T6** (needs files, effort M) Translate SyntHack/machine-45 anchors from 1.41 to 1.42 (byte patterns, not addresses) (tool: [`scripts/anchor_translate.py`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/scripts/anchor_translate.py), 2026-11-11: you supply both images; it reports per address whether the translation is exact, bracketed, one-sided or ambiguous)
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

- [hw] Boot unpack limit: the bootstrap loads compressed section 3 at `0x40200000` and unpacks it to `0x40000400`. The margin (decompressed minus compressed) must stay below ~`0x1FFC00` at every point of the stream. Stock 1.41 has a margin of +99,938 B. A build padded with zeros to `0x40350000` (-8,751 B) did not boot, tested twice and hung on the logo. Zero padding is the worst case; already-compressed payloads raise the margin. SyntHack refuses builds under 4 KB of margin. `[hw]` — `syntakt#43e5b0cc` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L53) · Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)

- [hw] Where mod code lives at run time (SyntHack modarea, v0.8.1+): The OS image has only ~2 KB free, and everything after it is zeroed at boot. So mod code is appended to section 3 compressed (SHLZ, at `0x40348000 + offset`). At boot it is unpacked into the first 64 KB block of the OS heap: buddy allocator `0x4010350C`, 16 MB pool at `0x444E38C0`. The block is reserved by a call right after heap initialization, so it always gets index 0, and the OS never hands it out again. The ARP mod wrote and sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; leaving default carriers absent cut the emulated serialization from 24.8 M to 4.8 M instructions (81 % fewer). The slowness is a user report; the cost is `[emu]`, the wall-clock gain not yet measured. `[doc]` {synfact-lifecycle} ([I50](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i50-mod-data-written-for-default-settings-slowed-project-load-and-save)) — `syntakt#fc2bb25e` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:26](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L26) · Syntakt / Recovery (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`)

- [emu] Kit and project storage that round-trips through stock code (SyntHack kitstore/projstore): Kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track blocks go into 6 file bytes that stock's writer zeroes and its reader ignores. 256 bytes go into the project settings block (`+0x227..+0x3FF` is zeroed by the writer and ignored by the reader), behind an `SH` marker. Tests run the real writer and reader with and without the hooks. Zero must mean "default", because stock-saved files load as zero. `[emu]` {synthack-mods} — `syntakt#0516d4bc` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:137](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L137) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`

- [doc] What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re} — `firmware-container#ded70082` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:61](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L61) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)

- [doc] Syntakt (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`): if the OS still boots, flash the stock `.syx` via Transfer's Drop page (works even if a mod misbehaved); if not, MIDI interface with a 5-pin OUT to the Syntakt's MIDI IN ("USB doesn't work from the startup menu"), FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, Transfer SYSEX TRANSFER "OS Upgrade via device startup menu", tens of minutes at 31.25 kbit/s, the unit restarts itself. Avoid TRIG 2 (empty reset) and TRIG 3 (factory reset) in the startup menu - both erase data. Do a dry run of the DIN procedure with the stock OS before the first flash; flash only files for which `tools/unpack/eft.py info <file>` reports `checksums : ok`; no hardware results are reported on the page. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery} — `recovery#2934ea2d` [hardware/common/recovery.md:36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L36) · Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)

MAIN is 3,438,480 bytes, section 7 is 383,760 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff} — `syntakt#bdaad9d3` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:31](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L31) · Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
- [doc] Stock public Machine IDs are 0-44, stored as a BYTE in each track's machine payload (`P[t]+0xA2`); runtime records `R[t] = model + 0x6C + 0x3C0*t`, `P[t] = *(R[t]+0x10)`; the setter is at `0x40025594` (store at `0x40025620`). 505 parameter descriptors of 52 bytes; only MAIN digital tracks 0-7. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff} — `syntakt#86553c61` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L32) · Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
- [doc] Section 7 selector: a signed BYTE with a 46-entry map (negative -> 0, 0-45 kept, above 45 clamped to 45); stock maps 0-7 to the same-numbered engine family and 36->8, 37->9, 38->10, 44->11, everything else (incl. 45) to family 0. Stock tables: render pointers `0x400148F0` (12 entries), prep pointers `0x40014920`, the 46-byte map at `0x40014950`. A compact handoff moves MAIN `[0x80002000,0x800021B0)` through a 27x16-byte eDMA transfer (TCD47, channel 47); each track then receives a 20-byte copy into `T[t] = 0x80003C40 + 0x8E*t`. Dslot is 8 x `0x708` = 14,400 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff} — `syntakt#0efd67de` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:33](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L33) · Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
- [doc] Persistence confirmed statically: the current-kit Sound-v7 save/load keeps the machine byte (raw 0-45 and 255 retained, 46-254 map to 0); Pattern-v11 stores the byte at row `+0x2EC` and its restoration is not closed; Sound locks, p-locks, held trigs, migration, clipboard and undo not qualified. Evidence labels in that repo: confirmed by static analysis / verified in emulator (none for the whole device) / verified on hardware (none) / hypothesis. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff} — `syntakt#899e0c2a` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:34](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L34) · Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
- [doc] Open: safe executable storage for native DSP on "CPU 2" (the loader boundary is unresolved); composition with SY FM4 (engine 4, A-table entry overlap) and other descriptor mods; resource IDs 254-261 are unclaimed in the registry but have MIDI CCs, 505+ have no native allocation. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff} — `syntakt#799f60d4` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L35) · Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
- [doc] Two ColdFire MCF5441x (V4, EMAC, no FPU, ~250 MHz, so 166,667 cycles per 32-sample block), with 64 KB SRAM at `0x80000000`. RAM shared between the CPUs is at `0x10000000`. `[doc]` — `syntakt#9f88239a` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:38](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L38) · Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
- [doc] Boot: entry `0x400004E8`; static constructors loop `0x40082500` (136 entries); the intro animation task `0x40087E6A` gates boot, so never make the intro longer. Screen: 128x64 1 bpp, column-major, double buffer at `0x402D6DC4`/`0x402D6DC0`; frame loop `0x4000A0E6` redraws when `*(0x444E1334)+96` is set. `[doc]` — `syntakt#3245b484` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:73](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L73) · Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
- [doc] CPU #2 (section 7): all work runs in the audio interrupt `0x40000934` (vector 96, DMA timer 0 capture). Per block it copies `0x1B0` bytes of parameters from shared RAM and renders 8 digital voices (`0x40004324`). It returns 8 x 32 int32 over eDMA channel 47 and does no mixing. 12 engines: tables at `0x400148F0` (render), `0x40014920` (update), `0x40014950` (machine id -> engine). Order: BD MODERN, SD BASIC, CY ALLOY, PC CARBON, SY TONE, SY CHORD, SD VINTAGE, CP VINTAGE, SY TOY, SY BITS, SY SWARM, SP TWINSHOT. SY CHORD reads a 512 x int32 wave at `0x4001A300`. `[doc]` — `syntakt#3d42d4e8` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:76](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L76) · Syntakt / Audio path
- [doc] CPU #1 (section 3): the per-block routine `0x400A3856` runs CV/gain, ADC deinterleave, then master/FX `0x4008F1CA`. Delay `0x40096890` and reverb `0x40096E3C` are the same code as on the Digitakt mk1. Buffers: digital tracks from CPU #2 at `0x80003D50`. ADC channels at `0x80003950`: 0-3 analog tracks, 4-5 external in, 6-7 the FX-track bus. USB/Overbridge: 20 channels per frame at `0x80004760`. The final mix is analog: digital buses go out through DACs into an analog mixer, with nothing digital after them. 40 control voltages go out over DSPI1 with eDMA channel 15; CV 35/36 are the FX-track bus VCAs. `[doc]` — `syntakt#9e1d0250` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:80](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L80) · Syntakt / Audio path
- [doc] Section 7 is byte-identical in 1.41 and 1.42 (SHA-256 `daf6451c...783bc2`). It is ColdFire ISA-C with EMAC, MCF5441x-class: compile with `-mcpu=54418`, disassemble with `-m m68k:isa-c:emac`. CPU #2 has its own 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000` (SP `0x48000000`, entry `0x40001070`). `[doc]` — `syntakt#e773fe40` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:89](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L89) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] Only 39.8 KB is code (`0x40000404-0x40009f88`: boot, audio interrupt, voice loop, 12 engines, sample loader), followed by 284 KB of tables and data. Code room for mods is almost nil: ~318 bytes in small pieces remained after SynCrackd's images. — `syntakt#e1ec1d13` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:90](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L90) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] The sample pool is in CPU #2's RAM: 64 MB from `0x4004f750`, in BSS zeroed at boot. A 64-entry slot table `{u32 frames, u32 pointer}` is at `0x4404f754`. Format: 64 times `u32 frames` + big-endian int16 mono. The main CPU fills it at boot in 2 KB chunks through the shared window `0x800`, with an unchecked 16-bit index. This is the slow boot the manual mentions. Per slot at most 524,287 frames (10.9 s; positions are 20.12 fixed point). The stock UI limits slots to 5 s and "32 MB". — `syntakt#7abf02d7` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:92](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L92) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] Shared window (CPU #2 `0x0-0x1000` = main CPU `0x10000000`, chip select 0, 16-bit, one wait state): `0x000-0x1b0`: the parameter block, copied to `0x80008000` every block; `0x1b0-0x5b0`: 8 mono track buffers, sent by eDMA 47; `0x5b0-0x800`: unused by stock; `0x800-0x1000`: the sample chunk at boot. — `syntakt#584bee6c` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:97](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L97) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] SRAM `0x80000000`: 8 voices of 1,800 B, 8 mono int32 output buffers, 8 parameter blocks of 142 B. The highest static reference is `0x8000f670`, so treat SRAM as full. — `syntakt#e90b2942` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:102](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L102) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] SynCrackd replaces Twinshot (and CY ALLOY) with a 64-slot stereo sampler, loops, slices, time stretch and transient triggers. It is OS 1.42 only, alpha, tested in emulation and on one unit, MIT. — `syntakt#9b8573f4` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:104](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L104) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] Each change is stored with the SHA-256 of the original bytes, so a different OS version fails the build instead of crashing. Every mod runs in a Unicorn emulator next to the original code before flashing. Stock Unicorn gets signed fractional EMAC wrong (the audio comes out silent), so EMAC instructions are trapped and executed in Python from the NXP manual. Use CPU model "ANY" (the code needs FF1, MVS/MVZ, SATS). — `syntakt#1144e802` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:110](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L110) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] Hooks: replace at least 6 bytes with `jsr` plus `nop` padding, and the trampoline replays the replaced instructions. Save every register; replay replaced EMAC instructions first. If your code uses EMAC, set MACSR yourself and leave ACC0 at 0, because the OS sum routines start from it. One-time setup goes in a hook in the page initializer (`0x401885D2...`), never in boot time. — `syntakt#d4c263b4` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:113](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L113) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] Mod code: gcc/as with `-mcpu=54418`, no `.bss` (put variables in `.data`), no libgcc (`nm -u` empty). ColdFire limits: `muls.l` takes no absolute address, there is no `exg`, `movem` takes only `(An)`/`d16(An)`, short branches reach ±127 B. — `syntakt#56340605` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:117](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L117) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] Spare storage the OS saves without knowing: per track: engine word +106 (hidden id 72); per kit: unused words of the pattern kit at `*0x800030BC` (ids 0, 0x1A, 0x24, 0x27, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x37, 0x46, 0x38). Store values XOR their default, so old projects load with defaults; kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track kit blocks (Digitakt MIDI-track data, unused here); 256 bytes in the project settings file. A "free" parameter id can be an alias the OS shows in some modes, so audit it. — `syntakt#fee3a98a` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:119](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L119) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] UI internals: parameter descriptors at `0x4022D59C + 52*id`; page objects at `0x41B9F3C8` (44 B, 8 slots); per-parameter `std::function` objects at `0x41B9FA24 + 84*id` (+20 text, +36 icon, +68 style). Page 25 ("OB8") is a free Digitakt leftover. - [doc] Audio mods: Hook the mix function; keep the OS's EMAC `msac` sign convention (the result is -Σ g·x). Do nothing when there is nothing to do. Compute at 24 kHz where the sound allows it. Ramps must snap to their target or the effect never goes idle. Limit how far a modulated delay moves per block. Keep a cost-per-block regression test (count instructions with `UC_HOOK_CODE` after `ctl_flush_tb()`). — `syntakt#33df5f9d` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:126](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L126) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`

- [doc] The analog tracks reuse the Analog Rytm MKII's voice design. The voice control records have the Rytm MKII's format (command/depth word, start and target bytes, mode nibble, rate exponent and mantissa). The cymbal oscillator banks use the Rytm's scale (43.62 units per Hz) and load the Rytm's CH/CB CLASSIC values. So Rytm voice research applies here and back. `[doc]` (inferred from the shared formats) — `syntakt#61c6c351` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:156](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L156) · Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)

- [?] [doc] Safe boot: a bank moves CANDIDATE -> TRYING (written before any bank code runs) -> GOOD, set once AUDIO and the sample pool are ready and 150 UI ticks (about 5 s) have passed; a crash or power-off before that boots the previous GOOD bank or stock machines. Each bank names an exact core contract, and the core checks the stock bytes that LFO3 and MODULATION SKIP patch before any initializer runs. `[doc]`, rollback `[?]` (not yet tested on hardware).
